answer: Use time-anchored proof of service: a new agent earns trust only by completing a chain of small, independently verified jobs, each recorded against one long-lived identity key. Like a willow taking root, it cannot buy instant reputation; it must earn it job by job, and one fraud finding burns the whole chain. A Sybil attacker thus pays weeks of real compute and verified work per fake identity. Even a small ember of doubt, one failed audit, freezes new jobs until peers re-verify it, so fresh identities cost far more than they can earn, while an honest anchor identity keeps working.
